Slice: Pickups To Expire

Intent

The pickup expirer's to-do list: every tool currently set aside for a holder, with the date it must be collected by. The expirer works through the ones whose collect-by date has passed, so a set-aside the holder doesn't collect in time ends and the tool moves on to the next neighbor.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Pickup Expirer, a system processor in the Expire Hold slice (slices/expire-hold.md). No person or screen reads this list.
  • What the expirer does with it: it reads the set-asides that are due to expire, and issues Expire Hold for each.

Read Model / View

  • View: Pickups To Expire built from events: "Hold Fulfilled", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Pickup Expirer (Expire Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a set-aside joins or leaves shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside is due to expire is worked out when the list is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it becomes due from the first read after the midnight that ends its collect-by date.

The view keeps one row for every live set-aside; the query returns only those due to expire. HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
holdId HoldId Hold Fulfilled.holdId.
toolId ToolId Hold Fulfilled.toolId.
neighborId NeighborId Hold Fulfilled.neighborId: the holder.
collectByDate Date Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate, as recorded there. Never worked out here.
dueToExpire Bool Derived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after collectByDate (INV-PTE-2). Worked out when the list is read.

When a row leaves the view. A set-aside's row is removed when:

  • Tool Checked Out is recorded for its tool by its holder (matching toolId and neighborId);
  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired is recorded for its hold;
  • Tool Retired is recorded for its tool; or
  • Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for its holder.

Nothing puts a row back. A tool recorded lost is always on loan, so it is never set aside, and Tool Lost needs no rule here.

Queries

  • List set-asides to expire. Takes nothing. Returns every row whose dueToExpire is yes, with holdId, toolId, neighborId and collectByDate. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the expirer, which expires each one.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-PTE-1: A set-aside is on the list from Hold Fulfilled, with the collect-by date recorded on it.
    • One row per Hold Fulfilled; nothing else creates a row.
  • INV-PTE-2: A set-aside is due to expire once its collect-by date has passed.
    • This is worked out by comparing the collect-by date with today. No event marks the set-aside as lapsed.
    • The set-aside lapses at the start of the day after its collect-by date, in the shed's local time. On the collect-by date itself it is not due.
  • INV-PTE-3: When the holder checks the tool out, the set-aside leaves the list.
  • INV-PTE-4: When the holder cancels the hold, the set-aside leaves the list.
  • INV-PTE-5: When Hold Expired is recorded, the set-aside leaves the list.
  • INV-PTE-6: When the tool is retired or the holder closes their account, the set-aside leaves the list.
    • Both end the hold.
  • INV-PTE-9: A checkout by anyone other than the holder doesn't take the set-aside off the list.
    • After the cut-off, the next holder, or anyone if no hold is waiting, may check the tool out before Hold Expired is recorded (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-3b). The lapsed hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • INV-PTE-10: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

The pickup window runs regardless of whether the holder can collect: it doesn't pause while the holder is suspended or has an overdue loan (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8; Expire Hold). This list treats every set-aside alike.

The list has no screen; only the Pickup Expirer reads it.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Hold Fulfilled was recorded for Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill on 10 October, with a collect-by date of 13 October.

  • Tool set aside (INV-PTE-1)
    • Given: the list is empty
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1: the drill, Ben, collect by 13 October
    • Then: H1 is on the list, collect by 13 October, not due to expire.
  • On the collect-by date (INV-PTE-2)
    • Given: H1 is on the list, and Ben hasn't collected the drill
    • When: the list is read during 13 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is not returned: it isn't due yet.
  • Collect-by date passes (INV-PTE-2)
    • Given: H1 is on the list, and Ben hasn't collected the drill
    • When: the list is read after the start of 14 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is returned as due to expire. Nothing is recorded until the expirer acts.
  • Holder collects in time (INV-PTE-3)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben on 12 October
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Someone else takes a lapsed set-aside (INV-PTE-9)
    • Given: H1 is on the list and due to expire, and Cara's hold was waiting behind it
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Cara on 14 October
    • Then: H1 stays on the list, still due to expire. It leaves only when Hold Expired is recorded for it.
  • Holder cancels (INV-PTE-4)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Set-aside expires (INV-PTE-5)
    • Given: H1 is on the list and due to expire
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list. If Hold Fulfilled is then recorded for Cara's hold H2, H2 joins the list with its own collect-by date.
  • Tool retired (INV-PTE-6)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-PTE-6)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ben
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-PTE-10)
    • Given: H1 is on the list once
    • When: the same Hold Fulfilled for H1 is applied again
    • Then: H1 is still on the list once, with the same collect-by date.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-PTE-10). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a set-aside no longer listed: once a row has left, a later Tool Checked Out, Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired, Tool Retired or Neighbor Account Closed for it changes nothing.
  • The expirer reads a set-aside twice before Hold Expired lands: the list may return the same hold on two reads in a row. Expiring a hold once is Expire Hold's rule, enforced when it records Hold Expired; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Pickup Expirer. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds IDs and dates only. No names or emails.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. How soon a due set-aside is expired is Expire Hold's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, collectByDate.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs and the Hold Fulfilled convention.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The Pickup Expirer reads it and issues Expire Hold.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":1,"name":"Expire Hold","x0":274.25,"x1":418.25,"docHtml":"

Slice: Expire Hold

Intent

When a holder doesn't collect a set-aside tool by the end of its collect-by date, end their hold so the tool passes to the next neighbor in the queue, or becomes available to borrow. The system does this itself; no person decides it.

Trigger & Actor

Internally triggered. The Pickup Expirer, a system processor in this slice, reads Pickups To Expire every 5 minutes, at any hour, and issues Expire Hold for each set-aside whose collect-by date has passed. A lapsed set-aside is therefore expired within about 5 minutes of midnight, shed time. No person expires a hold; the shed manager doesn't cancel set-asides by hand. There is no screen.

Command / Input

Command: Expire Hold

A HoldId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's expiredAt is that same moment.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
holdId HoldId yes The set-aside hold to expire. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-EXP-10), fulfilled (INV-EXP-10), not ended (INV-EXP-3), and past its collect-by date (INV-EXP-2).

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Pickup Expirer, also in this slice, reading Pickups To Expire.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Expired → context Holds Read by: My Holds (the hold drops off), Tool Catalog (the set-aside ends), My Loans (the hold no longer waits), Holds To Fulfill (the tool can pass to the next hold), Pickups To Expire (the set-aside leaves its list), Pickup Notices To Send (an unsent pickup email is dropped), and Undelivered Notices (a failed pickup email's entry drops off).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes From the command.
expiredAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event never changes. Readers find the hold's tool and holder from its Hold Placed or Hold Fulfilled.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. It reads Pickups To Expire (slices/pickups-to-expire.md), specified in its own doc. Hold Expired ends the hold in My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices, each eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Expiry ends the hold, and the tool then passes to the next waiting hold (Fulfill Hold sets it aside, recorded as Hold Fulfilled) or becomes available. Afterwards the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool, at the back of the queue (Place Hold, INV-HOLD-7). The neighbor gets no message when their hold expires: the pickup email already gave the collect-by date. An expired hold doesn't count against the neighbor; only late returns count toward a flag (Neighbors To Flag). Those rules are owned by those slices; this slice records only Hold Expired.

  • INV-EXP-2: A set-aside expires only once its collect-by date has passed: from the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries (the set-aside date plus 3 days), read as recorded and never worked out here. On the collect-by date itself, the hold can't be expired.
  • INV-EXP-3: Only a set-aside still in force can expire.
    • A set-aside ends without expiring when the holder checks the tool out, the hold is cancelled, the tool is retired, or the holder closes their account. Then nothing expires.
    • Someone else checking the tool out doesn't end the holder's set-aside. Once the collect-by date has passed, another neighbor may check the tool out before Hold Expired is recorded (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool); the lapsed hold still expires.
  • INV-EXP-4: The window runs regardless of whether the holder can collect.
    • A holder who is suspended or has an overdue loan can't collect, and their set-aside expires on the same terms as anyone's.
  • INV-EXP-10: Only a hold that has been placed and fulfilled can expire.
    • A hold still waiting has no collect-by date and never expires.
  • INV-EXP-11: Expiring a hold that has already expired succeeds and records nothing.
    • Hold Expired ends the hold for good: the holder loses their place in the queue, and nothing reopens it. Other commands on an expired hold are refused hold-ended.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: set-aside lapses (INV-EXP-2)
    • Given: Hold Fulfilled was recorded for Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill (T1), collect by 17 October. Ben hasn't collected T1, and Cleo's hold H2 is waiting.
    • When: at 00:10 on 18 October, shed time, the Pickup Expirer issues Expire Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Expired is recorded for H1, with the time it was recorded.
  • On the collect-by date (INV-EXP-2)
    • Given: H1 is set aside, collect by 17 October
    • When: Expire Hold for H1 is handled at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: refused with pickup-window-open: "This hold's pickup window hasn't ended." No event is recorded.
  • Holder already collected (INV-EXP-3)
    • Given: H1 was set aside, and Tool Checked Out was recorded for T1 and Ben
    • When: Expire Hold for H1 is handled on 18 October
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-EXP-3)
    • Given: H1 was set aside, and Hold Cancelled was recorded for H1
    • When: Expire Hold for H1 is handled on 18 October
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Tool retired (INV-EXP-3)
    • Given: H1 was set aside, and Tool Retired was recorded for T1
    • When: Expire Hold for H1 is handled on 18 October
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Holder closed their account (INV-EXP-3)
    • Given: H1 was set aside, and Neighbor Account Closed was recorded for Ben
    • When: Expire Hold for H1 is handled on 18 October
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else checked the tool out after the cut-off (INV-EXP-3)
    • Given: H1 was set aside, collect by 17 October. On 18 October, before Hold Expired was recorded, Cleo checked T1 out (ending her own hold H2).
    • When: the Pickup Expirer issues Expire Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Expired is recorded for H1. Cleo's checkout didn't end Ben's hold; only Ben's own checkout would have.
  • Former holder takes a lapsed set-aside nobody waits for (INV-EXP-3)
    • Given: H1 was set aside for Ben, collect by 17 October, and no other hold is waiting. On 18 October, before Hold Expired was recorded, Ben checked T1 out.
    • When: the Pickup Expirer issues Expire Hold for H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No Hold Expired is recorded; Ben's checkout ended his hold.
  • Suspended holder (INV-EXP-4)
    • Given: H1 was set aside, collect by 17 October, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Expire Hold for H1 is handled on 18 October
    • Then: Hold Expired is recorded for H1, the same as for any holder.
  • Hold still waiting (INV-EXP-10)
    • Given: Cleo's hold H2 on T1 is waiting and has never been fulfilled
    • When: Expire Hold for H2 is handled
    • Then: refused with hold-not-set-aside: "This hold hasn't been set aside." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown hold (INV-EXP-10)
    • Given: no hold has ID H9
    • When: Expire Hold for H9 is handled
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found: "There is no such hold." No event is recorded.
  • Expired twice (INV-EXP-11)
    • Given: Hold Expired was recorded for H1
    • When: Expire Hold for H1 is handled again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing; the Pickup Expirer logs it with the hold ID and moves on. No person sees these reasons. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. hold-not-found (INV-EXP-10).
  2. If Hold Expired is already recorded for the hold, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-EXP-11).
  3. hold-ended (INV-EXP-3).
  4. hold-not-set-aside (INV-EXP-10).
  5. pickup-window-open (INV-EXP-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
hold-not-found There is no such hold. INV-EXP-10
hold-ended This hold has already ended. INV-EXP-3
hold-not-set-aside This hold hasn't been set aside. INV-EXP-10
pickup-window-open This hold's pickup window hasn't ended. INV-EXP-2

hold-not-found and hold-ended mean the same conditions as in Fulfill Hold and Cancel Hold. A missing or malformed hold ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a repeated Expire Hold for a hold already expired succeeds and records nothing (INV-EXP-11). The Pickup Expirer may read the same lapsed set-aside twice before Hold Expired lands; the second command is then a repeat.

Requests at the same moment: Expire Hold is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per tool. A cancellation or the holder's checkout landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands. After the cut-off, the former holder may still check the tool out if nobody else is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool); that checkout ends their hold, and a later Expire Hold for it is refused hold-ended.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. No email is sent on expiry.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the Pickup Expirer issues Expire Hold. No person or screen does. It is an internal automation command, not on the REST API, so it has no sign-in guard.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Expired holds no name or email: only the hold and the time.
  • Performance / SLA: the Pickup Expirer reads its list every 5 minutes, so a lapsed set-aside is expired within about 5 minutes of the cut-off. In that gap the next neighbor in the queue can already check the tool out (INV-CHK-3b).

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (this slice): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These match slices/place-hold.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/pickups-to-expire.md and the conventions for Hold Fulfilled. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Read model this slice's processor reads: Pickups To Expire (slices/pickups-to-expire.md): the set-asides whose collect-by date has passed, each with its holdId.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices. Fulfill Hold then sets the tool aside for the next waiting hold.

Open Questions

None.
